sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is the only 50-foot sheet of the atlas and shows the centre of Cranford. Alden Street runs along the top of the sheet and Miln Street along the left edge, with Union Avenue North running down the middle from Alden Street to the Central Railroad of New Jersey, where it becomes Union Avenue South. The street grid is drawn turned on the page, so that North Avenue West and North Avenue East cut across it on the diagonal and meet Union Avenue at the railroad. Eastman Street runs across the lower part of the main business block. The railroad cuts the sheet from lower left to upper right as a broad band of tracks, with the passenger station and a news stand on its north side and a tunnel marked beside the station. The business blocks are drawn in colour: brick stores along Union Avenue and North Avenue West, among them the Post Office, drug stores, a bank and the Cranford Trust Building; the Masonic Hall and Township Offices on the east side of Union Avenue; a motion picture house on North Avenue West; a bake shop and a print and oil storage building south of Eastman Street; and a lumber and coal yard (Walter Mooney Co.) on Walnut Avenue and South Avenue East. West of the centre, the Public Library and frame dwellings stand along Miln Street, and a row of auto repair garages and a laundry back on North Avenue West. The lower left of the sheet is largely blank, with blocks laid out but not built. Water pipes of 6, 10 and 12 inches are marked in the streets, and the printed scale bar reads 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Alden and Eastman are lettered without a suffix; today's Alden Street and Eastman Street.
Union Av. N. and Union Av. S. are today's Union Avenue North and South Union Avenue (OpenStreetMap also has North Union Avenue for the stretch beside the railroad).

Placed with five hand-picked junctions read from the water-pipe lines and block edges, because the streets are drawn mostly by lot lines and the detector found only one point; the fit is a similarity at 50 feet to an inch (about 7.85 pixels per foot).
The tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey are today's Raritan Valley Line.

Downtown Cranford at 50 ft, one part: Union Av, Alden, Eastman, Miln, North and South Avs, Central RR of NJ station. Placed by 5 hand-picked pipe/block junctions and 1 detected point; the modern rail line is 26 m off the drawn tracks.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the north-west part of Cranford at 100 feet to an inch, between Claremont Place at the top and Eastman Street at the bottom, and from Normandie Place and Hampton Street in the west to Prospect Avenue and Miln Street in the east. The Rahway River crosses the sheet twice, once on the left, where Hampton Street and Central Avenue run along its banks, and again in a wide bend through the middle, and Riverside Drive follows the river across the upper part, with a small park by the river. The northern blocks (112, 113, 41) hold regular lots of frame dwellings along Claremont Place and Orange Avenue. At the top right, the E. I. Goodrich Estate, with its glass greenhouses, and the Cranford Casino Club and The Riverside, a boarding hotel, occupy the large grounds between Casino Avenue and Prospect Avenue. The built-up area south of Springfield Avenue includes the Grant Public School, the First Church of Christ, Scientist, the Cranford Catholic Club, St. Paul's Methodist Episcopal Church on Alden Street, and an apartment building in block 31. Hampton Hall, a boarding house, stands on Hampton Street near Berkley Place on the west bank of the river, and a Canoe Club is marked on Central Avenue. Water pipes are shown in nearly every street. The sheet's top and bottom margins and the Cranford stamp, scale bar and map division stamp are the only unmapped areas.
notes: Bargos Place is lettered with the alternative '3rd St.' in parentheses.
Berkley Place is lettered with that spelling; today's Berkeley Place.
Holly, Alden and Eastman are lettered without a suffix; today's Holly Street, Alden Street and Eastman Street.
Hampton Hall and the Canoe Club are identified in the drawing only by their lettering.
North-west Cranford at 100 ft, one part: Claremont Pl to Eastman, Rahway River, Casino and Prospect Avs.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre and north-west of Cranford at 100 feet to an inch, between Claremont Place and Arlington Road in the north and the Central Railroad of New Jersey yards in the south, with Prospect Avenue on the left and Hamilton Avenue on the right. The drawing is turned on the page and fills the whole sheet. The Rahway River bends across the middle from the left edge, where Riverside Drive runs by it, to the railroad at lower right. The upper blocks (114, 28, 227, 32) are lots of detached frame dwellings along Claremont Place, Cranford Avenue, Sylvester, Forest Avenue and Arlington, with the Lynwold property at Forest Avenue. The Riverside Apartments stand on Riverside Drive at the left. Springfield Avenue crosses the sheet near the middle; south of it lie the Cleveland High School, the First Presbyterian Church, St. Michael's Roman Catholic Church and a block of garages and shops along Alden Street and Union Avenue North, including the Township Garage, Fire Department, Police Headquarters and auto repair buildings. Diagonally across the lower right, North Avenue East, Centennial Avenue and South Avenue East run beside the railroad, with the Public Service Electric Co. Cranford Power Station, Robbins and Allison storage and a row of small lots on the north side of the tracks. Lincoln Park lies at the right edge beyond the river. Water pipe sizes are lettered throughout.
notes: Centennial Av. is lettered with '(Lincoln Pl.)' in parentheses.
Sylvester, Miln, Alden, High and Chestnut are lettered without a suffix; today's Sylvester Street, Miln Street, Alden Street, High Street and Chestnut Street.
Madison Avenue is lettered 'Madison Av.' at the top edge.
The drawn rotation is about 38 degrees counter-clockwise from the page; the fit gives 3.98 pixels per foot.
Central Cranford at 100 ft, one part: Claremont Pl to the Central RR yards, Union Av N, Springfield Av. Union Av N junctions at Claremont and Springfield displaced (8 m), excluded.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the eastern edge of Cranford at 100 feet to an inch, along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, from Elizabeth Avenue and the roundhouse yard in the north to Thomas Avenue in the south. The railroad corridor, here broad with many parallel tracks and sidings, runs diagonally from lower left to upper right, with North Avenue East on its west side and South Avenue East on its east side. At the top, the Central Railroad of New Jersey round house No. 16 with its turntable and a second turntable by the Baltimore and Ohio passenger station stand in the yards; the Loveland and Sons Lumber and Mason Storage Co. yard and a sawing and planing mill lie between North Avenue East and the tracks. West of North Avenue East, the blocks along Elizabeth Avenue, John and Hamilton Avenue hold frame dwellings on narrow lots, with Trinity Episcopal Church near Forest Avenue and a lettered Arlington Road crossing the middle. East of the tracks, long narrow lots run between South Avenue East, Hollywood Avenue, Burchfield Avenue and Thomas, mostly built with small dwellings. Lincoln Avenue runs up the right edge, and a street east of the yards is lettered 'not opened'. Water pipes of 6, 12 and 16 inches are marked, and the compass at upper left shows the sheet turned on the page.
notes: Centennial Av. is lettered with '(Lincoln Pl.)' in parentheses.
Cummings and John are lettered without a suffix; Thomas is lettered 'Thomas (Av.)'. Today's Cummings Street, John Street and Thomas Street.
Lincoln Avenue at the right edge is today's Lincoln Avenue East; the first-pass fit gives a rotation of about -43 degrees, 5 degrees different from sheets 3 and 4.
East Cranford along the Central RR at 100 ft, one part: Elizabeth Av to Thomas, North and South Avs E; drawn about 5 degrees turned from sheets 3 and 4.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south of central Cranford at 100 feet to an inch, between the Rahway River and Lincoln Park in the upper part and Winans and North Lehigh Avenue at the bottom, from High and Mansion Terrace on the left to Thomas on the right. The river winds from the upper centre to the left edge, where a mill race and bridge cross it, and Lincoln Park West and Lincoln Park East run along the park, a wide open tract with a large building in block 238 and the Cranford Oil Stone Works Inc. on the river. Lincoln Avenue crosses the sheet from the lower left to Centennial Avenue and on to the right edge. The compact residential district south-west of Lincoln Avenue (blocks 244 to 260) is laid out in short parallel streets: Mansion Terrace, Broad, Stratford Terrace, an unnamed street lettered 'Pleasure Way', Lawn Terrace and Edgebrook Place, crossed by Elm and by North Lehigh Avenue at the bottom. Almost every lot holds a frame dwelling. At the right, the Lincoln School, with its auditorium, stands between Centennial Avenue and Thomas, and Cummings crosses at the top. A fire alarm box and numerous hydrants and water pipes are marked. Severin Court and Winans run across the lower right, where the blocks are only partly built.
notes: Broad, Elm, High, Chestnut, Cummings and Winans are lettered without a suffix; today's Broad Street, Elm Street, High Street, Chestnut Street, Cummings Street and Winans Avenue.
N. Lehigh Av. is today's North Lehigh Avenue.
Pleasure Way is lettered in parentheses on a short street between Stratford Terrace and Lawn Terrace; no modern name found.
The Lincoln School is lettered 'Heat: steam. Lights: elec.'; the large building in block 238 is lettered as fireproof construction.
South-central Cranford at 100 ft, one part: Lincoln Park, Lincoln Av, Mansion Terrace to Edgebrook Pl; sheet turned the other way (north about 39 degrees right of up).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south-west of central Cranford at 100 feet to an inch, between South Avenue West and the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the top and the Rahway River at the bottom, from Lincoln Avenue on the left to South Avenue East on the right. The drawing is turned on the page, so that Union Avenue South and Retford Avenue run across it as horizontal streets and Woodlawn Avenue and Washington, a short street, run up and down. The upper left is a regular grid of small frame dwellings in blocks 142, 141 and 29, with Mooney Lumber Co. Inc. mill department and the Cranford Dairy beside the tracks at the top, and a Gospel Tabernacle of the Christian and Missionary Alliance on the corner of Cherry. Below Retford Avenue the blocks turn diagonally along Grove, Walnut Avenue and High, which run from upper right to lower left toward the bottom corner, where Lincoln Avenue runs to the lower left. At the right, South Avenue East and Chestnut hold a mix of shops, St. Mark's African Methodist Episcopal Church, the First Baptist Church and the Standard Lumber and Supply Co. yard. Denman Road is lettered at the left edge. Dwellings are mostly detached frame buildings with outbuildings, and only the Rahway River at the bottom edge is labelled with a water name.
notes: Washington is lettered without a suffix; today's Washington Place. Union Av. S. is today's South Union Avenue (the horizontal street). Cherry, Grove, Chestnut and High are today's Cherry Street, Grove Street, Chestnut Street and High Street.
Lincoln Av. at the left edge is today's Lincoln Avenue West; the diagonal Lincoln Av. at the lower left is today's Lincoln Avenue East.
The drawn rotation is about +50 degrees from the page, close to that of sheet 10; the fit gives 3.94 pixels per foot.
South-west Cranford at 100 ft, one part: Union Av S, Retford Av, Grove, Walnut and High Sts.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the central-west part of Cranford along the Rahway River. The river enters at the right edge, makes a wide bend through the middle of the sheet and leaves at the lower left, and the streets on either side of it are drawn turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. The upper left holds the regular blocks 600, 601, 604, 605, 608, 609 and 610 between Stoughton Avenue, Dorchester Avenue and Denman Road, laid out in narrow lots with very few buildings. Walnut Avenue runs diagonally across the north bank of the river from the lower left to Lincoln Avenue, with a row of frame dwellings along each side. At the top, Lincoln Avenue carries the Sherman Public School (a large building marked as fireproof, with steam heat and electric light, and a pink-coloured annex), near block 144 and Grove Street. South of the river a second district of small frame houses lies between Bluff, Elm, Pine, High, Hawthorne and Hickory Streets, blocks 243 and 250 to 255, with Mansion Terrace curving along the right side down to North Lehigh Avenue at the bottom. Blake Avenue is drawn as a curved street marked 'not opened'. Six-inch water pipes, hydrants (D.H.), a fire alarm box near Walnut Avenue and a few pink and blue (brick, stone or tile) buildings are marked. The lower left is largely unsubdivided ground (block 610) and carries the compass rose and the scale bar, with an A-B match line. Several neighbouring sheets are referred to by the large numbers 6, 7, 10, 17, 20 and 25 at the margins. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Lincoln Av. here is today's Lincoln Avenue East; Hawthorne, Elm, Pine, High, Hickory and Bluff are lettered without a suffix (today Hawthorne Street, Elm Street, Pine Street, High Street, Hickory Street and Bluff Street); N. Lehigh Av. is North Lehigh Avenue.

Denman Rd. is lettered with '(Rahway Av.)' beside it on the east-west stretch and '(Av.)' on the diagonal; Hendricks is not in OpenStreetMap under that name (modern Marsh Street appears to run on its line, see sheet 10).
Green Av. does not exist in OpenStreetMap today; Blake Avenue is lettered 'not opened' where it curves past block 610 and the modern street follows the drawn line only approximately.

Junctions on High Street (with Elm, Pine, Hawthorne, Hickory and Bluff Streets) were 3 to 6 m off the drawn position in the fit and were left out; modern High Street appears displaced from the old line.

Cranford at 100 ft, one part: Walnut Av along the Rahway River, Mansion Terrace, Sherman School, blocks 600-610. High Street displaced against its modern line, left out; south-west corner without control.

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 9 is the main map of the western edge of Cranford, against the Garwood line. The grid of streets is drawn turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. Rankin Avenue forms the top edge along the Borough of Garwood township line, which is drawn as a dash-dot line, and above it the margin is lettered 'See Map of Westfield', with only the stubs of Pine, Beech, Oak, Locust and Spruce Avenues showing. Lexington Avenue runs down the left side along the borough boundary and is the diagonal edge of the built-up area. Roosevelt, Preston, Besler and James Avenues and New Street run down the sheet between Rankin and Hillcrest Avenue, crossed by Burnside Avenue, and the blocks between them (549 to 552, 219, 220, 555 to 558) are mostly long narrow lots with few buildings, the houses gathered along Burnside and Hillcrest Avenues. Below Hillcrest, blocks 559 and 560 face Union Avenue South and are densely built with frame dwellings; blocks 566 and 567 lie between Union Avenue South and Retford Avenue, with Livingston Avenue running between them, and blocks 568 and 606 are blank down to Stoughton Avenue at the bottom. Six-inch water pipes, telephone-pole marks and a fire alarm box are shown along the streets. In the lower left, west of Lexington Avenue, the sheet draws open ground in block 565 with the Fredrick E. Miller Farms and their outbuildings, and the scale bar. The heavy-bordered inset at the upper left, at 200 feet to an inch, is a separate part of the sheet and is not covered here. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Union Av. S. is today's South Union Avenue; New is New Street; Roosevelt, Preston, Besler and James are Avenues in OpenStreetMap.
Pine, Beech, Oak, Locust, Spruce, Hazel, Hemlock and Hickory are lettered only as short stubs in the Garwood margin along Lexington Avenue and the top edge; they were not used as control.
The inset at the upper left (Garwood and Westfield Township, block 565, at 200 ft to an inch) has no street junction and was not georeferenced.
Hillcrest Avenue junctions sit consistently about 2 m from the drawn centreline in the fit; the street may have been widened.
West Cranford at the Garwood line (Rankin to Stoughton, Lexington to New St) at 100 ft; top-left inset at 200 ft (Garwood/Westfield, block 565) not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at 200 ft, upper left: Garwood/Westfield township ground, block 565, See Map of Westfield (no street junction or other feature shared with modern data; needs a carried point from sheet 20 or 21 if a drawn feature matches).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers a residential district in the west of Cranford, between the Garwood borough line at the top of the sheet and Stoughton Avenue at the bottom, with New Street on the west and Lincoln Avenue on the east. The street grid is drawn turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. Johnson, Burnside, Benjamin, Hillcrest, Union Avenue South and Retford Avenues cross the sheet, and New, Marsh, Williams, Elise and Christopher Streets run between them; South Avenue cuts across the north-east corner, and Denman Road meets Lincoln Avenue at the south-east corner. The blocks are almost entirely small frame dwellings with outbuildings, set on narrow lots, with house numbers along every frontage; blocks 216, 217, 561, 562, 563, 569 and 570 are the most built up, while the southern blocks along Stoughton Avenue (568, 571, 572, 573) are still largely vacant lots. A row of attached dwellings stands on Johnson Avenue near Elise Street, and the Apostolic Faith Pentecostal Church is on Johnson Avenue near the west end. There are few other buildings of note: a poultry house and a few concrete block garages in block 218 off New Street. Six-inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets, with a twelve-inch main on South Avenue. The strip above the borough line is left blank with the note 'See Map of Westfield', since the Borough of Garwood was covered by another atlas; Rankin, Spruce, New, Myrtle and Willow Avenues are lettered there only as stubs. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Union Av. S. is today's South Union Avenue; Lincoln Av. is Lincoln Avenue West; Benjamin, Marsh, Williams, Elise and Christopher are lettered without a suffix (today Benjamin Street, Marsh Street and so on).

Hendricks, the short street between Retford and Stoughton Avenues, is not in OpenStreetMap under that name; modern Marsh Street appears to run on its line south of Retford Avenue (the Marsh Street / Stoughton Avenue junction was rejected, 14.6 m off).
Denman Rd. is lettered with '(Av.)' beside it.
Street sheet at 100 ft (to be detailed from the worker report).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the northwest of Cranford, between the Garwood borough line on the left and Eastman Street on the right, and between West End Place at the top and Miln Street at the bottom. The streets are drawn turned on the page, with north towards the upper right. The upper left holds a large area of long narrow lots (blocks 213, 214 and 121) between Division Street (also lettered Sampson Av.), Greaves Place, Spring Garden and Orchard, with Estelle Place cutting across and houses only along the lower streets. North Avenue West and Holly run diagonally across the centre from the Garwood line to the south-east, lined on both sides with frame dwellings, and include the Roosevelt Apts. near block 145. A small stream crosses the middle from the left and joins the Rahway River, which makes a wide loop on the right of the sheet; Orchard and Eastman Streets and Central Avenue lie along it. The top right has the blocks between West End Place, Pittsfield Place and Hampton (blocks 133, 134 and 34), more sparsely built. Along the lower left the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey run diagonally with P. Camillo and Co. contractors' storage yard on the south side, and South Av. W., Lincoln Av. and Burnside Av. continue on the Garwood side of the township line. A filling station stands at Miln Street at the bottom right. The strip at the left is lettered 'See Map of Westfield' and 'Borough of Garwood' and is left blank. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Greaves Pl. is lettered '(Woodlawn)' beside it and Division is lettered '(Sampson Av.)'; Pittsfield Pl. is today's Pittsfield Street and Lincoln Av. here is Lincoln Avenue West.
Spring Garden, Orchard, Hampton, Holly, Eastman and Miln are lettered without a suffix (today Spring Garden Street, Orchard Street, Hampton Street, Holly Street, Eastman Street and Miln Street).
Lincoln Avenue West, South Avenue West and the rail corridor at the lower left were not used as control: modern Lincoln and South Avenues West lie 15 to 25 m from the drawn lines.

The lower half of the sheet has little control (Holly / Orchard and Central Avenue / Eastman Street only). A hand-picked North Avenue West / Orchard Street junction disagreed with the fit by several metres and was left out.
North-west Cranford at 100 ft, Garwood line to Eastman, North Av W and Holly; south half has little control. Lincoln and South Avs W left out (displaced).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the north of Cranford south of the Rahway River, from Riverside Drive and the river at the top to Eastman Street, Norman Place and Beech at the bottom, and from Doering Way and Lafayette on the left to Hampton St. and Normandie Pl. on the right. The street grid is drawn turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. The Rahway River enters at the upper left through an inlet, bends across the top of the sheet and leaves at the right, with Riverside Drive following its south bank and Claremont Pl. (4th St.) and Normandie Pl. at the top right. A curved street system, Balmiere P'kwy (Washington P'kwy) with Riverview Ter. and Balmiere Rd. N. and S., encloses block 361 at the upper left; part of it is lettered 'not opened'. The main grid is formed by Springfield Av., Willow, Berkley Pl., Norman Pl., Spruce and Beech running across, and Tulip, West End Pl., Pittsfield Pl. and Hampton St. running down. Most of the sheet is built with small frame dwellings, and blocks 380 to 382 along Hampton Rd. and blocks 129 to 132 hold many pink-coloured (brick or tile veneer) houses; the area between Ariola Av. and Spruce (blocks 124 and 127) and the lots along Tulip are largely vacant. A small stream runs through block 135 at the lower right. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked along the streets. The block numbers 13, 21, 22, 29 and 3 at the margins refer to neighbouring sheets, and the strip above Riverside Drive is left blank with the street stubs Kensington, Richmond and Henley Av. lettered. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Claremont Pl. is lettered '(4th St.)', Tulip is lettered '(Washington Pl.)', Ariola Av. is lettered '(Tulip)' and Lafayette is lettered '(Pl.)'; Balmiere P'kwy is lettered '(Washington P'kwy)'.
Berkley Pl. is today's Berkeley Place; Springfield Av. is Springfield Avenue; Tulip, Willow, Spruce and Beech are today's Tulip Street, Willow Street, Spruce Street and Beech Street.
Ariola Avenue and the Balmiere roads are not in OpenStreetMap under these names; the Balmiere Parkway curves and Riverside Drive were not used as control.

The Claremont Place / Normandie Place and Doering Way / Lafayette Place / Springfield Avenue junctions were rejected by the fit (12 to 15 m off); the modern streets there do not follow the drawn lines.
The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from its neighbour sheet 11, so West End Place runs across the top of sheet 11 and down the middle of this one.
Springfield Av / West End Pl district south of the Rahway River at 100 ft; drawn turned 90 degrees from sheet 11.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north-central part of Cranford, between Pacific Av. at the top and Claremont Pl. at the bottom, and between Dunham Av. and Clinton Pl. on the left and Prospect Av. and Tuxedo Pl. on the right. The grid is drawn turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Two street systems meet along Orange Av. near the middle. West of it, Columbia Av. and Manor Av. (S. 7th St.) run diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, with S. 9th St. above them and S. 6th St. and S. 5th St. below, in blocks 367 to 371 and 830 and 831; these are long lots with houses on the street fronts, and the streets La Salle, Elmora Av. and Clay Av. cut across the lower left. Below Craig Pl. (8th St.) a regular grid of blocks 104 to 111 lies between Normandie Pl. and Orange Av., crossed by Frazier Pl. (7th St.), Maple Pl. (6th St.) and Day Pl. (5th St.), with Central Av. down the middle. East of Orange Av., Casino Av. and Tuxedo Pl. run down the sheet with Raleigh, Parker, Manor (Pl.), Linden, Maple and Claremont crossing them, and blocks 36, 37, 39, 40 and 119 to 120 are built with larger houses on generous lots. A small creek crosses blocks 119, 37 and 40. The top right (blocks 390, 392, 223) is mostly lots with few buildings, and Pacific Av. along the top is lettered 'not opened' in places. Fire alarm boxes, six-inch water pipes and hydrants are marked, and the margins carry the block numbers 12, 13, 14, 21, 23, 24 and 29 of neighbouring sheets and the compass and scale bar. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Several streets carry their numbered names in parentheses: Manor Av. (S. 7th St.), Craig Pl. (8th St.), Frazier Pl. (7th St.), Maple Pl. (6th St.), Day Pl. (5th St.), Claremont Pl. (4th St.), Casino Av. (Sylvania Pl.); Manor Av. is also lettered '(Pl.)' on the stretch east of Orange Av.
Pacific Av. is lettered 'not opened' on the left; the Pacific Avenue junctions fitted 4.7 to 5.0 m off and the street was left out of the control.
OpenStreetMap has Lasalle Avenue (not used as control here); Frazier Pl., Clay Av. and S. 5th, 6th and 9th Streets are not in OpenStreetMap under these names and were not used.

Normandie Pl., Orange Av., Casino Av. and Central Av. joined well with modern streets; the Columbia Avenue / Orange Avenue junction fitted 3.4 m off, which may be a realignment at the bend of Orange Avenue.
Columbia, Manor and Orange Avs district at 100 ft; Pacific Av left out (4.7-5 m off). Old numbered street names in parentheses.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers a residential district in the north-central part of Cranford, drawn turned on the page so that north points towards the upper left. The street grid is bounded by Haskins Avenue (Grand) and Pacific Avenue, both not opened, at the top and by Claremont Place and Arlington Road at the bottom. Union Avenue North, Garden Street, Cranford Avenue, Bloomingdale Avenue and Adams Avenue (Lincoln Avenue) run up the sheet in parallel, and Elizabeth Avenue crosses them diagonally from the lower left to the right edge, with Madison and Hamilton Avenues running down from it on the east. Along the left edge are Tuxedo Place, Prospect Avenue, Linden Place and Maple Place. The upper blocks (391, 392, 224, 226, 256) are laid out in long narrow lots with few buildings, and the strips near the top are marked 'not opened'. The densest building is in blocks 225, 117, 118, 25, 228 and 115 to 116 near Elizabeth Avenue, almost all small frame dwellings with outbuildings, a few of them in brick or concrete (coloured red and blue). A cluster of concrete-slab buildings stands on the east side of Adams Avenue, and a fire alarm box marks Elizabeth Avenue near Bloomingdale Avenue. Six-inch water pipe runs in most streets. A compass rose with a north arrow stands in the middle of the sheet near Garden Street. The adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins (24, 13, 5, 4). The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and the Map Division, Princeton University Library stamp and the scale bar are in the lower margin.
notes: Haskins Av. (Grand) is today's Haskins Avenue; Adams Av. (Lincoln Av.) is Adams Avenue; Fiske Ter. is lettered twice, with (Chester Pl.) west and (Laurel Pl.) east of Union Avenue North.
Manor Av. is lettered with '(Pl.)' beside it and is not in OpenStreetMap under either name.
Haskins Avenue, Pacific Avenue and Lenox Avenue at the top of the sheet are lettered 'not opened' in part; Garden is lettered without a suffix (today Garden Street).

Rejected in the fit: Arlington Road / Hamilton Avenue (14.6 m), Claremont Place / Union Avenue North (9.1 m) and Lenox Avenue / Tuxedo Place (14.3 m), where the modern streets are displaced from the drawn ones.
Cranford Township east at 100 ft: Haskins Av to Claremont Pl, Union Av N to Adams Av, Elizabeth Av diagonal.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the north-eastern edge of Cranford where the borough meets Roselle, a district dominated by railroad land. The sheet is drawn turned, with north towards the upper left. A broad belt of Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks, lettered as full of railroad tracks, runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper centre and widens into a yard at the bottom left, where a round turntable, a roundhouse with radiating tracks, a water tank, coal chutes, a sand house and a large shaded engine house or shop stand beside Lincoln Avenue. A second railroad crosses the lower part of the sheet from the left to the right edge, and another pair of tracks and a curving siding run down the east side. West of the tracks, along North Avenue East, small frame dwellings fill the blocks of Carpenter, Osborne and Bell Places (blocks 536, 537, 797, 519), together with a building near Carpenter Place in blue that is a masonry or special-use structure. Fire alarm and water pipe marks run along North Avenue East. East of the tracks, South Avenue East and the streets across the Roselle line (Wilson, Hale, Heinrich, Harding, Bartlett, Cox and Bryant Avenue) are laid out in long narrow lots with almost no buildings (blocks 542, 577, 581, 580, 576, 579, 575, 578, 591). The dash-dot borough line crosses the upper right and is lettered Borough of Roselle Line. A compass rose with a north arrow stands near the top right. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the lower left corner is crossed by the adjoining sheets 5, 18 and 24.
notes: Wilson (Linden), Hale (2nd Av.), Heinrich (3rd Av.), Harding (Union), Bartlett (2nd St.) and Cox (3rd St.) are lettered with the parenthesised old names beside them; Hale Street and Heinrich Street survive today.
Helen Pl. and Lincoln Av. (south of the yard) are lettered 'not open'; Helen Place, Bell Place and Richards are not in OpenStreetMap, and Lincoln Avenue is modern Lincoln Avenue East.
Richards is probably today's Richard Street.

Placed from the single Carpenter Place / North Avenue East junction with the configured scale; the modern North Avenue East and South Avenue East lines agree with the drawn streets across the sheet in an overlay.
North Av E / Carpenter Pl, Roselle line and Central RR yard at 100 ft; anchored on one junction (low confidence).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers a platted but almost entirely unbuilt tract in the east of Cranford and across the line in Roselle, in the south-east corner of the atlas. The sheet is drawn close to north-up, although the street grid runs diagonally across the page. A grid of long ten-block rows, named in pairs as Cox, Christian, Dermody, Dietz, Hory, Kaplan, Minor, Robins, Stiles and Weng, each with an old numbered name in parentheses (3rd to 12th Streets), runs from the upper right to the lower left and is crossed by Bryant, Ludlow (Lehigh Av.) and Baltimore Avenues. Block after block is divided into narrow lots with block numbers (590 to 594, 596, 597, 616 to 622, 643, 644, 652 to 654, 658, 659, 660, 661, 669, 701) but only about twenty dwellings and a poultry house are drawn, clustered in blocks 596, 619 and 622. A curved block (701) and Amsterdam Avenue bend around the lower right. A broad belt of railroad right of way, marked with the Lehigh Valley and Baltimore and Ohio railroads, sweeps in a curve across the top left and top right, with a smaller plat of Heinrich, Harding and Quine Avenues in the top left corner (block 585). A dash-dot line near the right edge is the borough line, lettered Borough of Roselle Line. Meeker Avenue, McClellan Street and Buchanan Street appear at the lower left where the sheet meets sheet 19. A compass rose stands at the left edge. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and the margins carry the numbers of adjoining sheets 15, 18, 19 and 27.
notes: Christian (4th St.) is modern Cristiani Street; the other rows keep their names today (Dermody, Dietz, Hory). Kaplan (8th St.) appears to be today's Myrtle Street, since the junction with Bryant Avenue fitted on that name.
Ludlow Av. is lettered with '(Lehigh Av.)' beside it; modern Ludlow Avenue.
Heinrich (3rd Av.), Harding (Union) and Quine (4th Av.) are lettered with old names in parentheses; Quine is not in OpenStreetMap.
Baltimore Avenue / Dietz Street, Dermody Street and Hory Street were not detected in the first-pass run.
Roselle tract at 100 ft (Cox to Weng, Bryant, Ludlow, Baltimore). Kaplan (8th St) taken to be Myrtle Street from the fit.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the south-eastern part of Cranford, from the Lehigh Valley Railroad and North Lehigh Avenue at the top to Hayes and Arthur streets at the bottom, with Centennial Avenue running down the centre-right of the sheet. The district is drawn close to north-up. At the top, a row of small frame dwellings lines the south side of North Lehigh Avenue between Mansion Terrace and Edgebrook Place (block 262), and further east an industrial block holds the Minute Jelly Inc. works, a waterproof cord company and several small factory buildings, some coloured red for brick and one noted as badly damaged by fire. The Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet below them, with a passenger station, a stop shed and a water tank beside Centennial Avenue. South of the railroad the blocks (611, 635 to 638, 639, 640) are laid out in long narrow lots and are mostly vacant, apart from a gymnasium marked as built from plans, and a few dwellings on Centennial Avenue. The densest building is around Wall Street, Cranford Terrace, Rose Street and Philips Street (blocks 646 to 648, 662 to 666), where small dwellings fill every lot, and along McClellan, Buchanan, Grant, Arthur and Hayes streets east of Centennial Avenue (blocks 649, 655, 667, 670, 673). A fire alarm box stands near Centennial Avenue and McClellan Street. Several lines of six-inch water pipe are marked. A compass rose stands at the lower left. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the margins carry the numbers of adjoining sheets 6, 8, 18, 19 and 25.
notes: Harris Pl. (Elm) is lettered with a parenthesised name; Smith (Maple Av.) and McGregor (Dunham) likewise. Elm Street and Hillside Avenue survive; Harris Place and Smith are not in OpenStreetMap.

Philips is lettered with one L; today's street is Phillips Street. Wall, Rose, Myrtle, McClellan, Buchanan and Grant are lettered without a suffix (today Wall Street, Rose Street, Myrtle Street, McClellan Street, Buchanan Street, Grant Street).

Centennial Avenue measured 2.5 to 4 m off the other points in the fit, and its junctions with Hillside Avenue, Myrtle Street and Buchanan Street were rejected (12 to 18 m), so the modern line of Centennial Avenue seems displaced from the drawn one.
South Cranford at 100 ft: N Lehigh Av to Hayes, Centennial Av, Wall St, Cranford Terrace. Centennial Av junctions 2.6-3.9 m off; three rejected.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers a broad strip of south-eastern Cranford between Lincoln Avenue at the top and the line of McGregor (Dunham) Street at the bottom, with the Lehigh Valley Railroad crossing the middle of the sheet from side to side. The sheet is drawn turned, with north towards the upper right (the compass rose is at the top left), although the street grid on the upper half is close to square to the page edges. Above the railroad, Severin Court (with a loop of private street), Woodside Avenue, Moen (Linden Av.) and Meeker Avenue run down the sheet, crossed by Park, Jahn Place and Winans; the blocks (582, 583, 586, 587, 588) hold scattered small frame dwellings, and cinder-block dwellings are marked near Severin Court. At the right, an oblique grid of Hale (2nd Av.), Heinrich (3rd Av.), Quine (4th Av.) and Harding (Union) holds blocks 575, 578, 584 and 589, with a factory (Universal Tool Co.) at the top right beside a street railway right of way, and a cluster of dwellings in brick and tile near Heinrich. Below the railroad, long blocks of narrow lots (612, 613, 614, 640, 641) lie between Park (Pl.), Myrtle, Moen and McGregor (Dunham) and are almost entirely vacant. At the lower right the sheet shows the north-west end of the Roselle tract drawn on sheet 16, with Coolidge (Union), Hory (7th St.), Kaplan (8th St.), Minor (9th St.), Robins (10th St.) and Bryant Avenue (blocks 615, 617, 623, 642, 702). Six-inch water pipes run in most streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the margins carry the numbers of adjoining sheets 5, 6, 15, 16, 17 and 19.
notes: Severin Ct. is lettered with '(Private St.)' on its loop and with '(Thomas Av.)' on its western leg; Moen (Linden Av.), Hale (2nd Av.), Heinrich (3rd Av.), Quine (4th Av.), Harding (Union), Coolidge (Union) and McGregor (Dunham) carry parenthesised old names. Hale Street, Heinrich Street, Quine Street, Meeker Avenue, Severin Court and Woodside Avenue survive today; Lincoln Av. is today's Lincoln Avenue East.
Park (Pl.) at the left edge below the railroad is lettered 'Park' with '(Pl.)' beside it.

In the fit, Hale Street (Hale / Heinrich 7.1 m, Hale / Lincoln Avenue East / Meeker Avenue 3.9 m) and Myrtle Street / Park Street (5.0 m) were displaced from the drawn lines and were left out; all ten control points lie above the railroad, so the lower half of the sheet is placed by extrapolation.
"Meon St." at the bottom edge beside sheet 19 is a misprint for Moen Street; kept as printed. Stiles St. is lettered at the bottom right beside Meeker Av.

South-east Cranford at 100 ft: Lincoln Av E, Severin Ct, Woodside, Meeker, Lehigh Valley RR; all control above the railroad, the lower half (Roselle wedge) extrapolated. Hale St and Myrtle/Park left out (displaced).

sheet-19-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 19 is the main map of the sheet: the southern tip of Cranford, a regular plat of long blocks that stretches from Buchanan Street at the top to Raritan Road and the Linden Township line at the bottom. The grid is drawn turned, with north towards the upper right, and its streets run square to the page. On the right, a column of blocks (668, 671, 674, 677, 680, 684, 690, 694, 698) lies between Cleary Avenue and Moen and is cut by Buchanan, Grant, Arthur, Hayes, Garfield, Harrison, Cleveland, Heins (Roosevelt) and McKinley streets; at the left, a second column (676, 679, 682, 683, 688, 689, 692, 693, 696, 697) lies between Cleary and Coleman Avenues, and Centennial Avenue runs diagonally down the left side, cutting the corners of blocks 682, 688, 692 and 696 into wedges. Every block is divided into narrow lots, and almost all are vacant: only a few dozen dwellings are drawn, in blocks 668, 674, 676, 679, 683, 697 and 698 and along Raritan Road, together with a few sheds, a building marked as ruins of a fire and a tile-roofed dwelling. The dash-dot line along the bottom is the township line, lettered Raritan Rd. and Township Line, and the strip below it is Linden Township, which the sheet leaves mostly blank, apart from block stubs. A heavy-ruled box in the top left corner holds the separate part 2, and the block labels 17, 18, 16, 19, 25 and 27 in the margins give the adjoining sheets. A scale bar and compass rose lie in the blank area at the left. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Heins (Roosevelt) is lettered with a parenthesised name. Garfield, Harrison, Cleveland, Heins and McKinley are not in OpenStreetMap (the area east of Moen Street was rebuilt as an industrial park); McKinley Street survives only as a service road.
Buchanan, Grant, Arthur, Hayes, Moen and the other cross streets are lettered without a suffix (modern Buchanan Street, Grant Street, Hayes Street, Moen Street).

Placed from four junctions (Cleary Avenue with Buchanan and Grant Streets, Coleman Avenue and Moen Street with Raritan Road), which agree to 0.2 m RMSE at 3.96 px per foot; no leave-one-out value is available and Centennial Avenue, realigned and crossed by the Garden State Parkway, was not used.

South Cranford at 100 ft, two parts: 1 main (Cleary, Moen, Coleman Avs, Hayes to Raritan Rd), 2 top-left block in a heavy box (McGregor (Dunham), McClellan, Buchanan) anchored on a hand-picked junction.

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is a block in the top left corner of the sheet, set off from the main map by a heavy double line on its south and east sides, and showing the south-eastern end of Cranford where it meets the Roselle tract. The part is a plat of long narrow lots arranged in four blocks (650, 651, 656, 657) between McGregor (Dunham) at the top, McClellan in the middle and Buchanan at the bottom, with Cleary Avenue along the left edge, Moen running down the middle and Meeker Avenue along the right edge, where Bryant Avenue joins it at a small angle. The top edge of the plat slopes. Two small groups of cross lots appear in block 650 and 651, and only a handful of dwellings are drawn, in three on Cleary Avenue (numbers 13 to 19) at the left, so the plat is almost entirely vacant. The margins carry the numbers of adjoining sheets 17 and 18 at the left and top and 16 and 27 along the heavy line at the right and bottom. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, at the same scale and rotation as the main map of the sheet.
notes: McGregor (Dunham) is lettered with a parenthesised name; McClellan and Buchanan are lettered without a suffix (modern McClellan Street and Buchanan Street). Moen Street is also lettered at the top edge beside sheet 18.

Placed from hand-picked junctions of Cleary Avenue with McClellan and Buchanan Streets (257 ft apart), anchored with the main part's scale and rotation; the two points agree to 0.9 m. Cleary Avenue is cut by the scan edge, so the junction centres were read from the block edge and the 60 ft street width. Low confidence.

South Cranford at 100 ft, two parts: 1 main (Cleary, Moen, Coleman Avs, Hayes to Raritan Rd), 2 top-left block in a heavy box (McGregor (Dunham), McClellan, Buchanan) anchored on a hand-picked junction.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the south-western corner of Cranford at 200 feet to an inch, along the Westfield and Clark township lines. A strip down the left edge, headed 'See Map of Westfield', carries numbered Westfield blocks (624 to 629) beside the Westfield Township line, and the Clark Township line runs south from it to Raritan Road at the bottom. In the upper left a grid of narrow streets, Connecticut, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, Carolina, North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia, runs east from Fairfield (Concord) Street, with Phillip, Morse and Concord Streets crossing it, a platted subdivision of blocks 813 to 826 that is almost empty apart from scattered dwellings, a steel water tower on the Mathias S. Toygevson lot and the Frederick Dechut and Frederick Demler houses along Lexington Avenue. A block belonging to the Picton Park Realty Co. is lettered in block 824. The double-track Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet from lower right to the left edge, with a siding, oil tanks, concrete coal silos and coal sheds beside it near Lexington Avenue. Lexington Avenue runs south from Denman Road (also lettered Rahway Av.) to Raritan Road, and Walnut Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from Raritan Road towards the north-east. Across the top right, Stoughton and Dorchester Avenues, Livingston Avenue, Marsh and Hendricks Streets bound blocks 598, 599, 602 and 603, divided into narrow lots with a few houses; Green Avenue and a fan of lots lie to the east, beside Walnut Avenue. The Rahway River makes a large loop in the lower right and the remaining blocks (606 to 610, 631 to 634) are unbuilt. Neighbouring sheet numbers 8, 9, 10 and 25 are printed in the margins.
notes: Denman Road is also lettered 'Rahway Av.' on the sheet; Fairfield is lettered 'Fairfield (Concord)'.

The Phillip, Morse, Concord and Fairfield grid in the upper left sits 15 to 25 m from the modern Phillips Street, Morse Street, Concord Street and Fairfield Avenue; those streets were left out of the fit.
Hendricks Street and Green Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap; modern Lenhome and Wilshire Drives, a replatting, occupy the unbuilt ground east of Lexington Avenue.
Lexington Avenue, Denman Road, Walnut Avenue, Raritan Road, Stoughton Avenue and Livingston Avenue still follow the drawn lines.
The Lehigh Valley Railroad is the modern Lehigh Line.
South-west Cranford at 200 ft: Lexington Av, Denman Rd, Stoughton, Livingston, Walnut and Raritan Rd; the west grid (Fairfield, Phillips, Morse, Concord) is 15-25 m off modern lines and was left out.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows the western edge of Cranford against the Westfield and Garwood boundaries, drawn at 200 feet to an inch. The Westfield Township line runs down the left side, and the bottom is cut by the Borough of Garwood and a note 'See Map of Westfield'. Two main roads cross the sheet on the diagonal: Division Avenue, continuing from Gallows Hill Road, and Brookside Place run south-west to north-east, with a fan of platted streets to the east and south, Waverly, Arnet, Hillside and Park, most of them marked 'Not Opened'. Orchard, Beech, Spruce, Ariola, Willow and Torbush Streets, with Tulip (Washington Pl.), run north-west to south-east between Brookside Place and Springfield Avenue, which bounds the east edge. Houses are built mainly in three places: along Division Avenue at the west edge, at the foot of the sheet around Cedar Street, 4th and 5th Avenues, and in the small blocks of Orchard, Tulip and West End Place in the south-east (block 122, with a fire alarm station). Wesighan Avenue (Prospect Av.), Mountain Sq. (Mountview) and Brookdale Place are laid out across large undivided tracts in the north, blocks 315 to 317 and 800, and Fairview Manor Farms and a group of farm buildings stand beside Springfield Avenue. A stream crosses the lower part of the sheet and 6-inch water mains are marked along several streets. The upper left is empty except for the compass and the Westfield Township line.
notes: Elizabeth Avenue is lettered with Morris Av. in parentheses; Wesighan Av. with Prospect Av.; Mountain Sq. with Mountview; Tulip with Washington Pl.; and a Tulip St. in parentheses stands east of Ariola Av.
Waverly Pl., Arnet Pl., Park Av., Spruce, Ariola Av. and Tulip south of Orchard are marked 'Not Opened'.
The north and west of the sheet have been replatted (Dartmouth Road, Harvard Road and others); Wesighan Avenue, Mountain Square, Division Avenue and Ariola Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap.

Modern streets that still follow the drawn ones include Brookside Place, Gallows Hill Road, Orchard Street, Beech Street, Torbush Street, Tulip Street, Spruce Street, Hillside Place, Arnet Place, Park Avenue, Cedar Street and West End Place.
The Waverly and Park Avenue junctions, and the Spring Garden, Lafayette Place and West End Place streets, differ from today's by 5 to 14 m and were left out of the fit.
West Cranford at 200 ft by the Garwood and Westfield lines: Brookside Pl, Orchard, Beech, Tulip, Torbush; the north (Wesighan, Mountain Sq, Division) replatted, extrapolated.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the Rahway River valley on the boundary between Cranford and Kenilworth, at 200 feet to an inch. Kenilworth Boulevard, 120 feet wide, crosses the sheet from the upper left to the right edge, with the Cranford and Kenilworth borough line running along it; the Rahway River and Norman Higgin Brook meet beside it. Springfield Avenue runs down the left side from the boulevard to the bottom corner and is the only built-up frontage on the sheet: a short row of dwellings and outbuildings stands on its east side near the foot, and a ruined building is marked 'Ruins of Fire' beside it. A tract of blocks 308, 309, 318 and 319 lies to the east of the river, unbuilt. In the lower right, streets of a platted subdivision, Glenwood, Edgewood, Ogden and Venetia Avenues, S. 4th Street and Laurel's Avenue, are laid out with 60-foot widths but carry no buildings; the Cranford and Kenilworth borough line turns south along the east side of this block. Doering Way and Riverview Terrace appear at the foot of the sheet. In the upper right, three long rectangular structures (shaded grey-blue) and a house stand beside the river, with the lettering 'Cranford & Kenilworth' and a pipe line. The Springfield Township line runs across the top. The compass and several neighbouring sheet numbers (12, 21, 23, 29, 33) fill the margins.
notes: Most of the sheet has no surviving street junction: Edgewood, Ogden and the other subdivision streets were replatted, and the modern Kenilworth Boulevard and Springfield Avenue junction sits about 60 m from the drawn one.
Placed from one hand-picked corner of the borough line, taken from sheet 23 where the same corner is drawn, with the scale and rotation assumed; low confidence.
Rahway River and Kenilworth Blvd at 200 ft, parkland; no usable junction; anchored on the borough-line corner at Laurel Av carried from sheet 23 (low confidence).

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the east-central part of Kenilworth, from the Rahway Valley Railroad on the north to Dunham Avenue on the south, drawn at 200 feet to an inch. Kenilworth Boulevard crosses the middle of the sheet from west to east; north of it Washington Avenue and Franklin Avenue (beside the Rahway Valley Railroad) cut across a grid of numbered streets, North 6th to North 15th Street, whose long narrow blocks 77 to 85 run from Washington Avenue down to the boulevard, with blocks 49 to 57 and 420 to 423 in the strip above. Houses are built in blocks 83 and 84 around North 7th, 8th and 9th Streets, where the First Baptist Church (Colored) stands, and the rest is vacant lots. South of the boulevard blocks 92 to 101 reach to the Cranford and Kenilworth borough line along Laurel Avenue; in Cranford south of the line the grid is South 4th to South 15th Street, with Manor Avenue and Columbia Avenue lettered over (S. 7th St.) and (S. 8th St.), and blocks 322 to 332, 343 to 346. Most of these blocks are empty; houses stand around Columbia and Dunham Avenues, where there is a pipe line along Columbia. In the lower left, a separate fan of narrow lots, blocks 341 and 363, lies between Venetia, Kensington and Richmond Avenues, with Clinton Place, Elmora and La Salle Avenues at the foot. A large frame building and a small circular structure, enclosed by an 8-inch water pipe, stand in the upper left beside the railroad.
notes: Manor Avenue and Columbia Avenue are lettered with (S. 7th St.) and (S. 8th St.) in parentheses; modern North 8th Street continues as Columbia Avenue.
Kenilworth Boulevard is named 'Boulevard' in OpenStreetMap; its junctions with the North streets lie 5 to 6 m off the Washington Avenue and Dunham Avenue rows and were left out of the fit.
The numbered South streets are not in OpenStreetMap; the south-west fan (Venetia, Kensington, Richmond Avenues) and the Edgewood and Ogden Avenues at the left edge were replatted.
The sheet's Rahway Valley Railroad is abandoned; the building and enclosure in the upper left are not named on the sheet.
Kenilworth at 200 ft (not 100): Washington Av, N 6th to 15th Sts, Columbia, Manor, Dunham. Boulevard (Kenilworth Blvd) junctions 5-6 m off, left out.

sheet-24-1.description: The main part of sheet 24, drawn at 200 feet to an inch, covers the large eastern section of Cranford Township lying between Kenilworth to the north, the Borough of Roselle Park to the east and North Avenue to the south; the Cranford Township and Borough of Kenilworth line runs down its east side and crosses the top. Most of it is a speculative street plan laid out on paper with very few buildings: long rows of narrow lots on Colonial, Rodman, Union, Home, Trenton, Cranford, Bloomingdale and Roselle Avenues in the north, crossed by Watchung, Birchwood, Cherrywood, Ashland and Pinewood Avenues, and on Albany, Adams, Van Buren, Wade, Raymond and Veronica Avenues in the south, crossed by Haskins, Henry, Bell, Lambert, Richards, Osborne and Carpenter. Many of these streets are marked 'Not Opened'. The north-west corner, along Belmont Avenue and the numbered South 9th to South 17th Streets, belongs to Kenilworth and is a little more built up, with the Roosevelt School on Pacific Avenue and a row of dwellings on South 15th Street. Small groups of frame dwellings stand on Orange Avenue, on Adams Avenue near Elizabeth Avenue, on Wade Avenue, and along Elizabeth Avenue down to a filling station at North Avenue, where a sixteen-inch water main is marked. Several streets carry an older or alternative name in parentheses, such as Haskins Av. (Grand) and Albany Av. (N. High). The lower-left corner, cut off by a heavy line, is a separate inset.
notes: Many of the paper streets of this sheet were never built as drawn or were replatted; the Garden State Parkway now crosses the east of the sheet. Control came from 14 junctions of streets that survive (Bloomingdale, Cranford, Roselle, Albany, Adams, Veronica and others).
Sailer Av. is today Sailer Street; Lambert is Lambert Street; Carpenter Pl. and Osborne Pl. keep their names.

The numbered Kenilworth streets carry their old names in parentheses: Minnisink (S. 16th St.), Stevenson (S. 17th St.), Savery (S. 18th St.), Lenape (S. 19th St.), Watchung (S. 14th St.), S. 10th (Forsythe), S. 11th St. (Claremont Pl.).
Faitoute Avenue / Summit Avenue and Adams Avenue / Haskins Avenue were detected 11 to 16 m from the fit and left out.
Cranford Township east (Albany, Adams, Van Buren, Raymond) at 200 ft; two parts: main and lower-left inset (Laurel Av, Belmont Av, S 15th to 19th Sts, Kenilworth side) cut off by a heavy line.

sheet-24-2.description: The lower-left corner of sheet 24, cut off by a heavy line, is an inset at 200 feet to an inch showing the western edge of Kenilworth west of Orange Avenue, which is otherwise not drawn on the street sheets. Laurel Avenue crosses the top of the inset and Belmont Avenue the bottom, with South 15th, 16th, 17th and 18th Streets running between them; Norfolk Avenue and South 19th and 20th Streets run diagonally towards Orange Avenue on the east side, where Newark, Passaic and Quinton Avenues and South 21st Street meet it. The borough line follows Laurel Avenue and Orange Avenue. The blocks (333, 334, 335, 751 to 755 and 116 to 121) are almost all vacant lots, with only a handful of dwellings on South 17th Street, on Belmont Avenue and near South 20th Street. Neighbouring sheet numbers 23, 24, 27, 32 and 14 are printed in the margins of the inset.
notes: Placed from two hand-picked junctions on Orange Avenue (Quinton and Passaic Avenues, 80 m apart) with the atlas scale for 200 ft sheets and the rotation of the main part: low confidence away from Orange Avenue.
The Laurel and Belmont Avenue blocks west of Orange Avenue were replatted after 1929 (today Coolidge Drive, Lee Terrace, Hemlock Street); no junction there survives.
Newark Avenue / Orange Avenue / South 21st Street was not used: it was also off on sheet 27 (8 m).
Cranford Township east (Albany, Adams, Van Buren, Raymond) at 200 ft; two parts: main and lower-left inset (Laurel Av, Belmont Av, S 15th to 19th Sts, Kenilworth side) cut off by a heavy line.

sheet-25-1.description: The main part of sheet 25 covers the south-western corner of Kenilworth and the adjoining part of Cranford Township, east of the heavy line that separates it from a 200-foot sketch of Cranford on the left of the sheet. The Cranford Township and Borough of Kenilworth line runs diagonally through it. In the north-east, Summit, Trenton, Union and Vernon Avenues and Woodland Avenue form a regular grid of narrow, almost entirely vacant lots in blocks 146 to 152, bounded on the west by Faitoute Avenue. West of Faitoute Avenue a second grid, set at an angle, carries Home, Trenton, Cranford, Bloomingdale and Roselle Avenues across large blocks (765 to 777) crossed by Ashwood Avenue; the only cluster of houses on the part is a row of small frame dwellings on both sides of Bloomingdale Avenue, and a short street marked 'Not Named, Not Opened' runs south of Roselle Avenue. The Rahway Valley Railroad curves across the southern part of the sheet. South of it, between Pinewood and Maplewood Avenues, lie long narrow lots on Park Place, Cherrywood, Beechwood, Ashwood and Oakwood Avenues, mostly vacant, with a few dwellings, a poultry house and coops, and a dance pavilion near Beechwood Avenue. Colfax Avenue along the bottom of the sheet follows the line of the Borough of Roselle Park, and Amsterdam Avenue is lettered at the bottom edge. Six-inch water pipes and hydrants are marked only along Bloomingdale and Vernon Avenues. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Vernon Av., east of Faitoute Avenue, is today part of Bloomingdale Avenue; old Union Av. and Cranford Av. meet Faitoute Avenue at one point and continue as Union Avenue and Cranford Avenue.

The angled blocks west of Faitoute Avenue (Trenton, Cranford, Bloomingdale and Roselle Avenues, Ashwood Avenue north of the railroad) have been replatted and the Garden State Parkway now crosses them; no control was taken there.
Colfax Av. is today West Colfax Avenue.
The Rahway Valley Railroad (R.V.R.R.) crossing the south of the sheet is no longer a running line.

Two parts: part 1 main (Kenilworth/Cranford Twp east of Centennial Av: Summit, Trenton, Union, Vernon, Faitoute, Bloomingdale, Roselle, Colfax; 100 ft); part 2 west of a heavy line at 200 ft (Cranford, High St, Rahway River, Raritan Rd, Centennial Av), turned about 54 degrees, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: left part at 200 ft west of the heavy line: Cranford south of the Lehigh Valley RR, Rahway River, tract 634, Raritan Road and the Centennial Avenue strip (sketch at 200 ft whose drawn streets (Centennial Avenue, Raritan Road, the stubs of sheet 17 streets) do not agree with modern lines at one scale and rotation; most of the area is drawn at 100 ft on sheets 17, 19 and 20; needs carried points from sheets 17, 19 and 20 once placed (step 6b)).

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the southern part of Kenilworth along the Cranford and Roselle Park borough lines, from Summit Avenue at the top to Colfax Avenue at the bottom, and from Michigan and Faitoute Avenues on the west to the Rahway Valley Railroad and the Union Township line on the east. The map is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the street grid, which runs at about 25 degrees to north, stands upright on the page. The upper half is a regular grid of long narrow blocks (numbers 148 to 179) between Michigan Avenue and Market Street, cut by Trenton, Union, Vernon, Woodland and Fairfield Avenues, almost wholly platted but vacant, with a scatter of frame dwellings on Union and Woodland Avenues and near Michigan Avenue. The Rahway Valley Railroad (R. V. R. R.) sweeps in a curve from the lower left across Faitoute Avenue and Market Street and then runs north along the east side of the sheet, with a triangular strip of blocks (numbers 187, 188, 210) beside it. The lower half holds blocks 126 to 128 and 181 to 186 between Lexington, Hamilton and Colfax Avenues, Faitoute and Maplewood Avenues, Myrtle and Willow Avenues and South 30th Street, laid out at odd angles where the Faitoute Avenue diagonal meets the grid, nearly all of it unbuilt. Linden borders the long block 187 with its narrow lots. The Borough of Roselle Park lies along the bottom edge, beyond the borough line in Colfax Avenue, and the dash-dot Union Township and Roselle Park lines run diagonally across the lower right.
notes: Market (lettered without a suffix) is today's Market Street.
Linden (lettered without a suffix) is today's Linden Avenue.
Hamilton Avenue, South 30th Street and South 31st Street are not in OpenStreetMap under those names.
Colfax Avenue is today's West Colfax Avenue.
Kenilworth at 100 ft, one part: Summit to Colfax Av, Michigan/Faitoute to Linden; Rahway Valley RR curve and Roselle Park line at the bottom.

sheet-27-1.description: The main part of sheet 27 covers the south-western quarter of Kenilworth, from Jefferson Avenue and Kenilworth Boulevard in the north to Summit Avenue in the south, and from Michigan Avenue in the east to Orange Avenue and South 20th Street in the west; a heavy line cuts off a 200-foot sketch of part of Cranford in the upper left. The east half is a regular grid of narrow lots between Kenilworth Boulevard, Kingston, Clinton, Monmouth, Newark, Passaic, Quinton, Richfield and Summit Avenues, mostly vacant, with scattered dwellings along Michigan Avenue. West of South 25th Street the numbered streets (South 21st to South 25th) run at an angle to this grid, and the built-up core lies around Newark and Passaic Avenues between South 23rd and South 25th Streets, with rows of small frame dwellings in blocks 141, 142 and 143. The New Orange Park Power House of the New Orange Park Water Company, with its pump, boiler room and artesian well, stands on Newark Avenue east of South 25th Street, next to a lumber yard and a saw mill; a small group of houses lies on Commerce and North 24th Street at the top of the sheet. Faitoute Avenue runs to the bottom edge, where the Kenilworth and Cranford borough line follows Summit Avenue, and the Orange Avenue side carries the borough line too. Water pipes of the New Orange Park Water Company are marked on several streets. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Richfield Avenue is lettered 'Richeield Av.' west of Faitoute Avenue, an engraving error; the reading keeps it as printed.
Commerce (lettered without a suffix) is today's Commerce Street.
S. 26th St. south of Richfield Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap under that name.
No control was found along Kenilworth Boulevard, whose junctions were not detected.

Two parts: main (Kenilworth, Kenilworth Blvd, Newark, Passaic, Quinton, Richfield Avs, S 21st to 26th Sts; 100 ft) and top-left part at 200 ft (Cranford: Grant, Arthur, Hayes, Garfield, Moen, McKinley, Raritan Rd; Berlant Development Co).

sheet-27-2.description: The upper-left part of sheet 27, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 200 feet to an inch, shows the south-eastern corner of Cranford along Raritan Road, west of the Kenilworth and Linden Township line. Moen Street runs down its west side, crossed by Grant, Arthur, Hayes, Garfield, Harrison, Cleveland, Heins and McKinley Streets, which end at large undivided blocks (669 to 699); these streets are drawn in full at 100 feet on sheet 19. East of them lies a large tract, block 661, marked William Meyer and Berlant Development Co., still vacant. Along Raritan Road at the bottom are the Grove Dairy Farm, with a dwelling and outbuildings, and a short row of small dwellings on McKinley Street at Berlant Avenue, which runs up the east side along the township line. Styles Street and Baltimore Avenue are lettered at the top edge. A note on Raritan Road refers to the Map of Elizabeth, Volume 2, for the ground to the south. The north arrow on this part is drawn straight up, but the fit puts north about 18 degrees to the right, in line with the neighbouring sheets.
notes: Placed from four points: Moen Street and Berlant Avenue on Raritan Road, and Moen at Harrison and at Cleveland carried from sheet 19 part 1 (RMSE 1.1 m); the inset fits about 4 percent smaller than 200 ft to an inch. Low to medium confidence.

Grant, Arthur, Hayes, Garfield, Harrison, Cleveland, Heins and McKinley are lettered without suffixes; the area east of Moen Street was later rebuilt as an industrial park (Commerce Drive) and most of these streets are gone.
'See Map of Elizabeth Vol. 2' is printed along Raritan Road.

Two parts: main (Kenilworth, Kenilworth Blvd, Newark, Passaic, Quinton, Richfield Avs, S 21st to 26th Sts; 100 ft) and top-left part at 200 ft (Cranford: Grant, Arthur, Hayes, Garfield, Moen, McKinley, Raritan Rd; Berlant Development Co).

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the north-east corner of the Kenilworth part of the atlas, from Jefferson Avenue at the top to Summit Avenue at the bottom, and from Michigan Avenue on the west to South 32nd Street on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees so that the street grid stands upright on the page. The west third is a regular grid of long narrow blocks (numbers 166 to 174) between Michigan Avenue and Market, cut by Kenilworth Boulevard, Kingston, Clinton, Monmouth, Newark, Passaic, Quinton and Richfield Avenues, almost entirely vacant apart from a few dwellings and the Rawhide Products Company, maker of fan belts and tire patches, at Kingston Avenue. The Rahway Valley Railroad (R. V. R. R.) runs the full height of the sheet beside Market, splitting into sidings that curve east to the factories. Beside it stand the Woolen Mill Products Corporation (block 191), Grady and Shrodes, anthracite coal processing (block 190), the Papyrus Company, paper converters, and the Protexol Corporation, makers of wood preserving oils, with a tank farm. East of the line the large blocks 205, 206 and 209 hold the American Circular Loom Company, makers of light wall tubing, and the Kenilworth Manufacturing Company, button manufacturers, each with its own spur. At the top, a pond lies above N. 26th Street, with a pump house and a car shed and depot near the railroad. Water pipe is marked in several streets, and the stamp of the Princeton University Library Map Division overlies the lower right.
notes: Market (lettered without a suffix) is today's Market Street.
Kenilworth Boulevard junctions were not detected; control rests on the avenues and Market.
Kenilworth at 100 ft, one part: Jefferson to Summit, Michigan to S 32nd; factories along the Rahway Valley RR.

sheet-29-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 29 is the upper, Cranford half of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the street grid, which runs about 59 degrees off north, appears at an angle on the page; its own arrow points to the upper left. It is headed Cranford and ends at the heavy line that crosses the sheet below Riverside Drive, with the Rahway River winding along its western side. The block grid is formed by Venetia, Kensington, Richmond and Henley Avenues running down the page from upper left to lower right, crossed by Edgar Avenue (with the old name Apgar in parentheses) and Franklin Avenue, with Clinton Place at the right and Glenwood Avenue and Ogden Avenue at the upper left. Riverside Drive closes the lower edge along the heavy line, and Claremont Place (lettered with 4th St. in parentheses) runs across the lower right. The blocks (numbers 339, 340, 362 to 366 and 320) are cut into narrow lots and carry scattered frame dwellings, a few of them in colour, with the densest building along Richmond and Henley Avenues. The river makes a loop at the left and flows out below Riverside Drive. Sheet numbers 22, 23, 12 and 13 name the neighbouring sheets. The 6-inch water pipe is marked along Riverside Drive, Franklin Avenue and Claremont Place.
notes: Edgar Avenue is lettered 'Edgar Av. (Apgar)'; Apgar is the old name.
Claremont Place is lettered with '(4th St.)' as an old name.
Glenwood Avenue and Ogden Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap under those names and carry no control (Glenwood Road and Glenwood Terrace exist today).
Edgar, Kensington and Claremont junctions with Riverside Drive were not detected; control rests on Edgar, Richmond, Henley and Franklin.

100 ft, two parts 1.5 km apart: 1 Cranford (Venetia to Clinton Pl, Edgar Av to Riverside Dr); 2 Kenilworth works at N 7th St (Kayden Co, Adams Laundry Machinery) placed from two points carried from sheet 30.

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is the lower, Kenilworth half of the sheet, below the heavy line that crosses the page, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It is an industrial area on the Rahway River, which sweeps across the upper left and down the left edge. The G. L. Kayden Company, makers of chemicals, paints and varnishes (admission refused), occupies the open ground west of the river bend with a row of long buildings of corrugated iron on steel frames, served by water pipe and hose connections. To the east and south stands the large plant of the Adams Laundry Machinery Company, Inc., manufacturers of washing machines, with sheet metal works, storage, machine shop, wood working department, pattern storage and office, and a south warehouse at the foot of the sheet. A web of sidings of the Rahway Valley Railroad (R. V. R. R.) crosses the plant from east to west. At the right edge Sheridan Avenue, North 7th Street, Monroe Avenue and Franklin Avenue are drawn where the works meet the Kenilworth street grid, with the United Engineering Company as lessee north of the plant. The sprinkler system, pipes and hydrants are marked in detail. Neighbouring sheets 22, 23 and 30 are named around the margin. Control is two junctions carried from sheet 30, so the placement is approximate.
notes: No modern junction survives here; the part is placed from North 7th Street / Sheridan Avenue and North 7th Street / Monroe Avenue carried from sheet 30.
North 7th Street meets Sheridan and Monroe Avenues only on the 1929 map; OpenStreetMap has no junction there.

100 ft, two parts 1.5 km apart: 1 Cranford (Venetia to Clinton Pl, Edgar Av to Riverside Dr); 2 Kenilworth works at N 7th St (Kayden Co, Adams Laundry Machinery) placed from two points carried from sheet 30.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the northern part of Kenilworth, from Black Brook and the Union Township line along the top edge to Franklin Avenue at the bottom, and from North 7th Street at the left to North 15th Street at the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid close to upright on the page. Concord Avenue runs along the top below the brook, Lafayette Avenue and Sheridan Avenue cross the middle, and Monroe Avenue, Washington Place and Franklin Avenue close the bottom, each cut by the numbered cross streets North 8th to North 15th Street. The blocks are numbered 15 to 29 in the northern tier and 406 to 419 in the southern; the northern blocks are cut into narrow lots and almost entirely vacant, while the area around Sheridan and Monroe Avenues carries scattered frame dwellings, a church on block 27 and a coal yard at the curve of the railroad. The Rahway Valley Railroad (R. V. R. R.) enters at the lower left on a diagonal of sidings and sweeps in a broad curve across Halsey and Monroe Avenues to run east along the bottom of the sheet beside Franklin Avenue. The brook winds along the top and turns down the right side with the Springfield Road line, and a second stream runs down the left edge. Water pipe is marked in Sheridan and Monroe Avenues. The sheet joins sheet 29 on the left and sheet 31 on the right.
notes: Halsey (lettered without a suffix) is today's Halsey Street.
Concord Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap and carries no control; Lafayette Avenue appears only from North 14th Street eastward.
Halsey Street / North 13th Street and Franklin Avenue / North 13th Street were not detected.
Kenilworth at 100 ft, one part: Concord to Franklin Av, N 7th to N 15th.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the middle of Kenilworth, from Delaware Avenue and Concord Avenue at the top to Monroe Avenue at the bottom, and from Springfield Road and North 15th Street on the left to Commerce and the Rahway Valley Railroad on the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid close to upright on the page. The western two thirds is a grid of long narrow blocks (numbers 7 to 14, 30 to 34, 301 to 307 and 37 to 43) between North 15th and North 22nd Streets, cut by Concord, Lafayette, Sheridan and Monroe Avenues, and mostly vacant, with dwellings scattered along the lower streets and a Methodist Episcopal church lettered Kenilworth M. E. Church on block 39. A single heavy line of the Rahway Valley Railroad crosses the sheet in Center, lettered R. V. R. R. At the upper left a large building with a storage shed, drawn in blue, stands on Springfield Road at the head of block 7, with the brook crossing just below. East of North 19th Street a large undivided tract (blocks 202 and 203) borders College Avenue, Webster Avenue and Oak and holds the American Keystone Corporation, with an office, a long building marked as proposed, a pump house, a water tower and a hall, and a radio broadcasting station, W. I. B. S., further north. The railroad curves along the right edge. Water pipe is marked in Monroe Avenue and the cross streets. The sheet joins sheet 30 on the left, 32 below and 33 above.
notes: Center, Oak and Commerce (lettered without a suffix) are today's Center Street, Oak Street and Commerce Street.
Delaware Avenue, Concord Avenue, College Avenue and Webster Avenue have no modern junctions here and carry no control.
Center Street / North 22nd Street was rejected by the detector (10.9 m); the rails run in Center.
Kenilworth at 100 ft, one part: Delaware/Concord to Monroe, N 15th to Commerce. Center St has rails (Center/N 22nd rejected).

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the central and most built-up part of Kenilworth, from Monroe Avenue at the top to Newark Avenue and Laurel Avenue at the bottom, and from North and South 15th Street at the left to Commerce at the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid close to upright on the page. Kenilworth Boulevard crosses the middle of the sheet, with Washington Avenue above it and Clinton Avenue below, and the numbered cross streets run from 15th to 23rd, North of the boulevard and South of it. The densest building is in blocks 63, 64, 70, 71 and 72 between Washington Avenue and Kenilworth Boulevard east of North 18th Street, where rows of frame dwellings, stores, a post office and a fire house stand on narrow lots. West of that the blocks (58 to 61, 73 to 76, 102 to 106) are largely vacant, apart from the Harding School with its auditorium and the McKinley School nearby. Cross cuts diagonally across the upper left, beside the Charles Frost greenhouses (block 61), which are drawn in blue. A municipal garage and a gospel hall stand south of the boulevard near South 21st and 22nd Streets, with an auto sales building at South 19th Street. Water pipe is marked in the avenues and several cross streets. The borough line is drawn along Laurel Avenue at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Cross and Commerce (lettered without a suffix) are today's Cross Street and Commerce Street.
Monroe Avenue is drawn only as the top boundary street; its junctions here sat 2 to 5 m off the modern line and were left out of the fit.
South 15th to 19th Streets west of Orange Avenue were replatted (Coolidge Drive, Lee Terrace, Hemlock Street); none of their junctions are used.
Kenilworth Boulevard is called Boulevard in OpenStreetMap west of South 20th Street.
The street lettered Cross runs diagonally across the upper left; the first letter is a C, not a G.
Kenilworth at 100 ft, one part: Monroe to Newark/Laurel, S 15th to Commerce; Monroe Av (top boundary, half drawn) left out; west of S 18th replatted.

sheet-33-1.description: The main part of sheet 33 is a small-scale map, at 400 feet to an inch, of the northern and eastern outskirts of the Borough of Kenilworth, filling in the ground around the street sheets of the borough, whose areas are shown only as outlines keyed to sheets 26, 27, 28, 31 and 32. It reaches from Chester Avenue and the Union Township line in the north to Summit and Fairfield Avenues on the Roselle Park line in the south. The Rahway Valley Railroad runs north to south through the middle. West of it a strip of streets is outlined: Columbus and Delaware Avenues with North 16th to 19th Streets, College Avenue, and Center, Monroe, Washington, Federal and Jefferson Avenues on North 22nd, North 24th, Commerce, Michigan and North 26th Streets. East of the railroad the sheet is mostly open land: large tracts crossed by the West Branch of the Elizabeth River and its tributaries, and the Galloping Hill Park and Golf Course along Galloping Hill Road, with a few scattered buildings. South 31st and South 32nd Streets with Boulevard, Clinton and Newark Avenues mark the edge of the built-up blocks. Tracts marked S-4 to S-7 cover the open ground. Coloured lines along the boundaries of the street sheets show which sheet covers each area. The Union Township line runs round the north and east of the borough.
notes: Drawn at 400 feet to an inch; the fit through 12 junctions has an RMSE of 6.7 m, so the placement is approximate (low confidence).
Michigan Av. north of Kenilworth Boulevard is today North Michigan Avenue; Center is Center Street.
Galloping Hill Park is today part of the Union County park system (Galloping Hill Golf Course).
Kenilworth outskirts at 400 ft to an inch (Galloping Hill Rd, Elizabeth River, Union Township line, Chester Av); lower-left part at 200 ft by a heavy line. Sparse.
placenames: Galloping Hill Park and Golf Course

sheet-33-2.description: The lower-left part of sheet 33, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 200 feet to an inch, shows a small piece of Cranford on the Westfield Township line, west of the Rahway River parkland of sheet 22. Springfield Avenue enters from the west and forks into Kenilworth Boulevard, running north-east, and a second branch of Springfield Avenue curving south. The ground is open: large tracts numbered 308 and 315, with a few dwellings and outbuildings along Springfield Avenue near the township line. The Westfield Township line runs diagonally across the part, and the ground beyond it is marked 'See Map of Westfield'.
notes: Placed from a single hand-picked point at the fork of Springfield Avenue and Kenilworth Boulevard, with the atlas scale for 200 ft sheets and north taken as straight up the page (the part's own north arrow): low confidence; check its rotation against sheets 21 and 22.
The modern fork has been rebuilt; the drawn branches agree with today's roads only near the junction.
Kenilworth outskirts at 400 ft to an inch (Galloping Hill Rd, Elizabeth River, Union Township line, Chester Av); lower-left part at 200 ft by a heavy line. Sparse.
